chuckwagon.subject: Chuckwagon
chuckwagon.location_scope: Western cattle-drive ranges, Texas to the northern plains; an explicitly reconstructed mobile kitchen
documented_features: Goodnight's 1866 adaptation placed a pantry with shelves and drawers at the rear of an army wagon; a hinged door became a worktable and a lower boot held heavy cooking equipment [S1].

The archival photograph shows wooden spoke wheels, straight-sided wagon beds, canvas hoops, supply boxes and cooking equipment on an open range. Its catalog date spans approximately 1880-1910, so it supports construction form, not an exact pre-1900 paint scheme [S2].
Chuckwagons accompanied cattle work during the approximately 1866-1900 open-range era [S3].
documented_colors: Natural warm timber, cream unbleached canvas, dark iron tires and black cookware are material-colour reconstructions. No original maker's paint scheme is claimed from the monochrome image [S1][S2].
chuckwagon.render_brief: An unoccupied Western cattle-drive chuckwagon, 1866-1900, reconstructed as a compact static mobile kitchen. Four wooden spoked wheels with narrow iron tires and projecting hubs support a straight-sided wooden wagon bed on two axles; the rear wheels are slightly taller than the front pair. Three curved wooden hoops support a partly folded cream canvas tilt over the forward cargo. At the rear, a broad rectangular wooden chuck box has open shelves, small drawers and a hinged drop-front lid lowered horizontally as a worktable. A shallow heavy-equipment boot sits directly below the box. Show two black cast-iron pots and a plain tin coffee pot securely resting on the shelf. Use full natural warm timber grain, cream canvas, black iron and silvery tin, with no invented maker's paint or logos. A simple wooden tongue projects from the front, resting on a support. All sides complete; wheels connect to real axles. No people, animals, fire, stovepipe, automobile tires, suspension springs or modern gas equipment. This is a documented type, not an exact replica of Goodnight's first wagon.
chuckwagon.history_lesson: In 1866 Charles Goodnight adapted an army wagon into a mobile kitchen with a rear pantry and fold-down worktable. Chuckwagons carried food and equipment for cattle-drive crews; this model reconstructs the type rather than a surviving first wagon.

sources.title: National Park Service, The Chuckwagon, Grant-Kohrs Ranch
sources.supports: Documents Goodnight's 1866 adaptation, rear pantry shelves and drawers, hinged worktable, lower equipment boot and cast-iron cooking vessels. The displayed wagon is identified as a replica.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Cowboys sitting by supply wagons, approximately 1880-1910
sources.supports: Archival photograph supports wooden spoke-wheel running gear, wagon bed, canvas hoops and supplies; monochrome and broad dating do not authenticate a particular 1880s paint scheme.

sources.title: National Park Service, Chuckwagon Flip the Story
sources.supports: Places chuckwagons and cooks alongside cowboys, trail bosses and wranglers in the approximately 1866-1900 open-range cattle era.

uncertainties: Dimensions, exact wheel proportions, canvas folding, container layout and unpainted finish are disclosed reconstruction. No factory colour scheme or exact surviving wagon identity is asserted.
The source photograph includes people and animals; the model deliberately omits them. Its broad date range is supplemented by NPS documentation of the 1866-1900 wagon type.
